chosen_property.label: timestamp

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: targetCollection
candidates.comment: A specific collection relation between an update action and the collection of things that is the target of the action. Also called "collection to update", "target set", "destination collection". Examples: "The add action has targetCollection a list of items", "The update action's targetCollection is a database table", "This action modifies a targetCollection of documents.". Distinct from object, which is a more general target of an action.

candidates.label: collection
candidates.comment: A target relation for an update action, indicating the collection that is being updated. Also called "target collection", "updated collection", "collection object". Examples: "Add item update action collection 'Shopping Cart'", "Remove item update action collection 'Wishlist'".

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: targetUrl
candidates.comment: A URL identifying a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node URL", "educational standard URL", "learning objective URL". Examples: "The alignment object has targetUrl 'http://example.com/algebra-standard'", "The educational framework node's targetUrl points to its definition", "This targetUrl links to a specific competency."

candidates.label: targetDescription
candidates.comment: A textual description of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node description", "educational standard description", "learning objective description". Examples: "The alignment object has targetDescription 'Understand basic algebra'", "The educational framework node's targetDescription explains the competency", "This targetDescription details a specific learning outcome."

candidates.label: targetName
candidates.comment: A textual name of a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node name", "educational standard name", "learning objective name". Examples: "The alignment object has targetName 'Algebra I'", "The educational framework node's targetName is 'Critical Thinking'", "This targetName identifies a specific skill."

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: source

Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: energyEfficiencyScaleMin
candidates.comment: An energy efficiency scale minimum relation between energy consumption details and the lowest energy efficient class on the regulated EU energy consumption scale. Also called "lowest efficiency class", "worst energy rating", "bottom efficiency grade". Examples: "Energy consumption details energyEfficiencyScaleMin 'D'", "Product details energyEfficiencyScaleMin 'G'", "Appliance energyEfficiencyScaleMin 'E'". Distinct from energyEfficiencyScaleMax, which specifies the most efficient class.

candidates.label: hasEnergyConsumptionDetails
candidates.comment: An energy consumption detail relation between a product and its energy efficiency information. Also called energy efficiency details, energy rating details, consumption specifics. Examples: "A refrigerator has energy consumption details.", "An appliance has energy consumption details for its class.", "The product's energy consumption details are listed."

candidates.label: area
candidates.comment: An area relation between a broadcast service and the geographic place where its users can access it. Also called service region, coverage area, broadcast zone. Examples: "A radio station's area is 'Greater London'.", "The TV service's area is 'North America'."

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: claimReviewed

Distinct from error, which provides general information about the cause of failure.

candidates.label: availableIn
candidates.comment: An administrative area where a drug strength is available. Also called: market availability, regional availability. Examples: "DrugStrength '500mg' availableIn 'US'", "DrugStrength '10mg' availableIn 'EU'."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: negativeNotes
candidates.comment: Negative considerations or drawbacks associated with a product or described in a review. Also called cons, disadvantages, downsides, criticisms. Examples: "Product X negativeNotes 'short battery life'", "Review Y negativeNotes 'poor customer service'", "Software Z negativeNotes 'steep learning curve', 'frequent crashes'". Distinct from positiveNotes, which describes favorable aspects.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: seeks

candidates.label: competencyRequired

Also called "required skill", "prerequisite competency", "learning outcome". Examples: "Certification competencyRequired 'Problem-solving skills'", "Course learning resource competencyRequired 'Basic algebra'".

candidates.label: requirements
candidates.comment: A requirements relation between a software application and the necessary components or environments for its operation. Also called system requirements, dependencies, prerequisites. Examples: "A video game has requirements 'Windows 10, DirectX 12'.", "A Java application has requirements 'Java Runtime Environment 8+'.", "A design software has requirements 'macOS 10.15, 8GB RAM'."

candidates.label: supply
candidates.comment: A resource relation between a how-to guide or direction and a consumable supply required for its execution. Also called "required supply", "consumable item", "material needed", "ingredient". Examples: "The recipe has supply flour", "The how-to direction requires supply glue", "This guide lists several supply items.". Distinct from tool, which refers to a non-consumable instrument.

candidates.label: requiredQuantity
candidates.comment: A required quantity relation between a how-to item and the amount of that item needed. Also called quantity needed, amount required. Examples: "A how-to item 'sugar' has a required quantity '1 cup'.", "A crafting project needs a required quantity '5 sheets of paper'.", "A recipe step specifies a required quantity '2 eggs'."

candidates.label: dependencies
candidates.comment: A prerequisite relation between a tech article and the requirements needed to fulfill its steps. Also called: technical requirements, prerequisites, required components. Examples: "Software Installation Guide" dependencies "Python 3.8, pip", "Hardware Setup Article" dependencies "Screwdriver, Internet connection", "Programming Tutorial" dependencies "Basic understanding of algorithms".

candidates.label: physicalRequirement
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the physical activities or abilities required for a job posting. Also called physical demands, fitness requirements, job physicality. Examples: A job posting has a physical requirement of 'ability to lift 50 lbs'. A job posting has a physical requirement of 'standing for long periods'. A job posting has a physical requirement of 'manual dexterity'.

candidates.label: qualifications
candidates.comment: A qualification relation between a job posting or occupation and the specific credentials or skills required. Also called required skills, job requirements, eligibility criteria. Examples: "A software engineer job posting requires qualifications like a 'Bachelor's degree in Computer Science'.", "A doctor's occupation requires qualifications like 'Medical License'.", "A project manager role requires qualifications like 'PMP certification'."

candidates.label: softwareRequirements
candidates.comment: A dependency relation between a software application and other software, text, or URLs specifying necessary components for its operation. Examples: "Game X has softwareRequirements DirectX 12", "This application's softwareRequirements include Java Runtime Environment", "The softwareRequirements list specific operating system versions."

candidates.label: coursePrerequisites
candidates.comment: A requirement relation between a course and the conditions or prior knowledge needed to take it. Also called: prerequisites, required courses, entry requirements. Examples: "Advanced Algorithms" course prerequisites "Data Structures", "Calculus II" course prerequisites "Calculus I", "Graduate Seminar" course prerequisites "permission of instructor".

candidates.label: parentOrganization

Distinct from subOrganization, which points from a larger organization to its smaller components.

candidates.label: superEvent

Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". candidates.label: subOrganization

candidates.label: subEvents

Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: subTrip

Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: partOfTrip

candidates.label: partOfSeries

candidates.label: greater

candidates.label: partOfOrder

candidates.comment: A remaining attendee capacity relation between an event and the number of available spots for attendees. Also called available seats, remaining tickets, open spots. Examples: "A concert has a remaining attendee capacity of 100.", "A workshop has a remaining attendee capacity of 5.", "A conference has a remaining attendee capacity of 500."

candidates.label: maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A physical attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can physically attend. Also called: in-person capacity, venue limit, on-site capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 500", "Live Concert maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 10000", "Workshop maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 30". Distinct from maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity, which refers to online attendees.

candidates.label: maximumAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: An attendee capacity relation between an event or place and the total number of individuals it can accommodate. Also called: maximum occupancy, total capacity, attendee limit. Examples: "Concert Venue maximumAttendeeCapacity 5000", "Conference Room maximumAttendeeCapacity 100", "Public Park maximumAttendeeCapacity 10000".

candidates.label: maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A virtual attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can attend online. Also called: online capacity, virtual participant limit, streaming capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 2000", "Webinar maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 500", "Online Class maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity 100". Distinct from maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity, which refers to in-person attendees.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: rsvpResponse
candidates.comment: The specific response (e.g., Yes, No, Maybe) provided to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply. Examples: `Wedding RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Yes`, `Conference RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: No`, `Party Invitation` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Maybe`.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

instances: Donald Trump -> Volodymyr Zelensky

chosen_property.label: knows
chosen_property.justification: knows matches Person→Person for a meeting intention

candidates.label: meetsEmissionStandard
candidates.comment: An emission standard compliance relation between a vehicle and the qualitative value, text, or URL indicating the emission standard it meets. Also called: emission compliant, environmentally certified, low emission. Examples: "Electric Car meetsEmissionStandard 'Zero Emission'", "New Diesel Car meetsEmissionStandard 'Euro 6'", "Hybrid Vehicle meetsEmissionStandard 'CARB LEV III'".

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: doorTime
candidates.comment: A door time relation between an event and the date or time when admission will commence. Also called "admission time", "entry time", "gate opening time". Examples: "Concert event doorTime '19:00'", "Theater show doorTime '2023-11-01T18:30'", "Festival doorTime '10:00'".

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: contactPoint
candidates.comment: A communication relation between a health insurance plan, organization, or person and one of their contact points. Also called "contact info", "point of contact", "reach at". Examples: "Company organization contactPoint 'Customer Service'", "Person contactPoint 'Email Address'". Distinct from contactPoints, which is the plural form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: contactPoints
candidates.comment: A communication relation between an organization or person and their various contact points. Also called "contact information", "points of contact", "ways to reach". Examples: "Company organization contactPoints [Customer Service, Press Office]", "Person contactPoints [Email, Phone]". Distinct from contactPoint, which is the singular form, though semantically similar.

instances: Donald Trump -> Volodymyr Zelensky

chosen_property.label: spokeOnPhone
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that one person spoke on the phone with another person.
chosen_property.justification: no existing schema.org property captures a phone conversation between two persons

candidates.label: speakable
candidates.comment: A designation of sections within an article or webpage that are highlighted as particularly suitable for text-to-speech conversion. Also called "text-to-speech section", "audible content", "read-aloud section", "speech-optimized content". Examples: "The news article has speakable the main body text", "This webpage's speakable sections are identified by CSS selectors", "The speakable content is specified by a URL fragment."

candidates.label: telephone
candidates.comment: A textual representation of the telephone number for a contact point, organization, person, or place. Also called "phone number", "contact number", "telecom number". Examples: "The organization has telephone +1-555-123-4567", "The person's telephone is 555-987-6543", "The place lists its telephone number."

candidates.label: servicePhone
candidates.comment: The contact point, typically a phone number, used to access a service. Also called service contact number, service hotline, phone access. Examples: `Customer Support Channel` servicePhone `ContactPoint: 1-800-XXX-XXXX`, `Emergency Service Channel` servicePhone `ContactPoint: 911`, `Booking Service Channel` servicePhone `ContactPoint: Local Booking Line`. Distinct from `telephone`, which is a general phone number for an entity.

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: serviceSmsNumber
candidates.comment: The contact point, typically a phone number, used to access a service via text message (SMS). Also called service text number, SMS access, text message service. Examples: `Customer Support Channel` serviceSmsNumber `ContactPoint: 555-TEXT-HELP`, `Alert Service` serviceSmsNumber `ContactPoint: 222-ALERTS`, `Booking Service` serviceSmsNumber `ContactPoint: 444-BOOK`. Distinct from `servicePhone`, which is for voice calls.

candidates.label: transcript
candidates.comment: A transcript relation between an audio or video object and the text of its spoken content. Also called audio text, video text, spoken content. Examples: "AudioObject transcript 'Hello, welcome to the podcast.'", "VideoObject transcript 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.'", "Lecture recording transcript 'Today we will discuss quantum physics.'".

candidates.label: faxNumber
candidates.comment: A fax number relation between a contact point, organization, person, or place and its associated fax telephone number. Also called: facsimile number, fax line. Examples: "Acme Corp" fax number "+1-555-123-4567", "Dr. Smith's Office" fax number "555-987-6543", "Public Library" fax number "555-111-2222".

candidates.label: contactPoints
candidates.comment: A communication relation between an organization or person and their various contact points. Also called "contact information", "points of contact", "ways to reach". Examples: "Company organization contactPoints [Customer Service, Press Office]", "Person contactPoints [Email, Phone]". Distinct from contactPoint, which is the singular form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: callSign
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a broadcast service, person, or vehicle and its unique callsign. Also called "radio identifier", "station ID", "vehicle identifier". Examples: "Radio station broadcast service callSign 'KEXP'", "Amateur radio operator person callSign 'W1AW'", "Aircraft vehicle callSign 'N123AB'".

candidates.label: contactOption
candidates.comment: A feature relation for a contact point, indicating an available option such as a toll-free number or accessibility support. Also called "contact feature", "available option", "support option". Examples: "Customer service contact point contactOption 'TollFree'", "Accessibility contact point contactOption 'HearingImpairedSupported'".
